history.dynasty: Pallava (7th-8th c. founding); Chola (12th c. main shrine, 1178-1216); Vijayanagara; later Nayaka-period gali gopuram
history.period: 7th-8th century origins; present structure 12th century; gopuram 18th-19th century
history.summary: One of Nellore's oldest temples, on the south bank of the Penna (Pinakini) river in Ranganayakulapeta. Legend says sage Kasyapa performed a yagna here on Ekadasi day, Vishnu appeared and stayed, and Adisesha took the form of the Talpagiri hill that serves as the Lord's couch; the Ramayana's Aranya Kanda is said to mention Rama's visit during his exile. Stone inscriptions date the present main shrine and mandapams to Chola kings (1178-1216), with Vijayanagara rulers adding gopurams and mandapams. The 70-ft, seven-storey Gali Gopuram with seven gold-plated kalashams was built in the late 18th-19th century - sources conflict on the exact date (1781 vs 1879, by Yeragudipati Venkatachalam Pantulu). The 10-ft reclining idol faces west toward the river, and the sanctum walls are inscribed with the Vishnu Sahasranamam. DUPLICATE: seq 1221 refers to the same temple as seq 26 (Talpagiri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Nellore); id kept unique.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple (Talpagiri)
town_description: Nellore, on the banks of the Penna river in southern coastal Andhra Pradesh, is the headquarters of Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district. A historic rice-trading and aquaculture centre, it is known for its ancient Vaishnavite and Shaivite temples, including Talpagiri, Jonnawada and Narasimhakonda.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, about 170 km away; Chennai International Airport is a longer alternative.
travel.railway: Nellore railway station, about 3-5 km away, on the Chennai-Vijayawada line.
travel.road: About 3 km from central Nellore; on NH-16, about 175 km north of Chennai; auto-rickshaws and buses from the bus stand.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Brahmotsavam in March-April is the grandest festival period.
